decision: Credit policy is versioned; every decision records the version that made it
why: Regulators and customers ask 'why was I declined in March'; the answer is a version, not today's rules.
value: Any past decision is reproducible, and rollback is one click.

decision: Rules render as readable cards (bands, installments, exceptions), not JSON
why: Policy owners are risk people, not engineers; they should review the actual rule text.
value: Reviews focus on the policy, not the syntax.

decision: Changes are reviewed as a diff with removed and added values highlighted
why: Reviewers approve changes, not whole documents; a diff shows exactly what moves.
value: Faster, more precise approvals, borrowed from code review.

decision: A draft must be replayed against the last 30 days before approval is requested
why: Approvals and losses move together; the replay puts both numbers in front of the approver.
value: No policy ships without its expected cost.

decision: Publishing needs a second approver who is not the author, and conflicting rules block it
why: Credit policy changes can move millions; separation of duties is a control, and overlapping rules make decisions order-dependent.
alternative: Single approver with an audit log.
value: Mistakes and conflicts are caught before customers see them.
